  <section v="18">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Based on the earlier explanation that the virtue of Torah study for its own sake is not only about self-nullification but also about the study being in a manner of "I do not know," this applies to the level of "I do not know," which then affects the subsequent knowledge, making it entirely different, ultimately uniting the limited intellect with the unlimited Torah and with the Holy One, blessed be He.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And according to what was explained above, that the virtue of Torah study for its own sake is not only in the matter of self-nullification, but also that a person's study is in a manner of "I do not know,"</t>
    <t s="1">it can be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that this is also the case regarding the level of "one who does not know,"</t>
    <t s="3">that this brings about</t>
    <t s="4">(afterwards)</t>
    <t s="5">upon her also in the knowledge</t>
    <t s="6">[for Torah study must specifically be with understanding and comprehension],</t>
    <t s="7">that he understands with his intellect matters in the Torah that previously he had no connection to.</t>
    <t s="8">And as explained by his honor, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, in one of the sichos of Purim,</t>
    <t s="9">that by reaching the level of "I do not know,"</t>
    <t s="10">the knowledge that comes afterwards is in an entirely different manner.</t>
    <t s="11">And in general, it is that the limited intellect of man becomes united with the unlimited Torah that he studies,</t>
    <t s="12">and through this he also becomes one with the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="13">Israel, the Torah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, are all one.</t>
  </section>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on the earlier explanation that the virtue of Torah study for its own sake is not only about self-nullification but also about the study being in a manner of "I do not know," this applies to the level of "I do not know," which then affects the subsequent knowledge, making it entirely different, ultimately uniting the limited intellect with the unlimited Torah and with the Holy One, blessed be He.

translations.translation: And according to what was explained above, that the virtue of Torah study for its own sake is not only in the matter of self-nullification, but also that a person's study is in a manner of "I do not know,"
that this is also the case regarding the level of "one who does not know,"
upon her also in the knowledge
[for Torah study must specifically be with understanding and comprehension],
that he understands with his intellect matters in the Torah that previously he had no connection to.
And as explained by his honor, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, in one of the sichos of Purim,
that by reaching the level of "I do not know,"
the knowledge that comes afterwards is in an entirely different manner.
And in general, it is that the limited intellect of man becomes united with the unlimited Torah that he studies,
and through this he also becomes one with the Holy One, blessed be He,
Israel, the Torah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, are all one.
